learning_objectives: Explain the role of each C in improving Al outputs.
Apply the 3 Cs to write clear, structured prompts.

slides.title: Title Slide
slides.narration:
Welcome to this Spoken Tutorial on The 3
Cs of Prompting.
slides.image_prompt: Title Slide

slides.title: Learning Objectives Slide
slides.narration:
In this tutorial, you will learn to
define, explain, compare, and apply the 3
Cs of prompting.
slides.image_prompt: Learning Objectives Slide

slides.title: System Requirements Slide
slides.narration:
Here I am using a browser on a computer
or mobile.
slides.image_prompt: System Requirements Slide

slides.title: Pre-requisite Slide
slides.narration:
To follow this tutorial, you must be
connected to the internet.
should also be familiar with what a prompt
is.
No coding needed.
slides.image_prompt: Pre-requisite Slide

slides.narration:
Have you ever got a strange answer from
an AI?
That's because of a weak prompt.
A weak prompt gets a weak answer.
A strong prompt gets a smart answer.
slides.image_prompt: Person sitting at a laptop, thinking before typing

slides.narration:
Best prompts include three ingredients:
1. Clarity,
2. Context, and
3. Constraints.
slides.image_prompt: Show graphic to explain

slides.narration:
Let's start with the first C — Clarity.
The Al can't read your mind.
When you explain your thoughts clearly,
the Al gives better results.
slides.image_prompt:
Section Header: 1. Clarity
Person at laptop, thought bubble above
head, Al with a question mark

slides.narration:
A clear prompt usually has these
elements:
• A well-defined task or goal
• A clear topic or focus, and
• Any special instructions for the Al to
follow
slides.image_prompt:
Icons representing “task”, “topic",
"instructions", "details"

slides.narration:
If these aspects are missing, your prompt
becomes vague.
And vague prompts lead to vague answers.
slides.image_prompt: Person scratching head, confused at vague | instruction

slides.narration:
Lets Open any Al tool for example,
ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, or the one you
usually use.
Type a vague prompt in the message box
and submit it.
slides.image_prompt:
Screen recording showing browser with
different Al tools (ChatGPT, Gemini,
Claude)

slides.narration:
For example, consider this prompt. "Write
about electric cars."
What do you think, is this clear or vague?
Think about it.
What should the Al focus on?
Audience?
Length?
It doesn't say what aspect to focus on.
slides.image_prompt:
On chatGPT Close-up: user typing "Write
about electric cars"

slides.narration: The output will be broad and unfocused.
slides.image_prompt: Al generating long generic text

slides.narration: Now, let's improve it.
slides.image_prompt:
Screen close-up: user typing improved
prompt

slides.narration:
"Write a short blog post explaining the top
3 benefits of owning an electric car for
someone living in a city."

See the difference?
The output is sharper, more relevant, and
structured.
slides.image_prompt:
Side-by-side: vague output vs improved
output

slides.narration:
Now, let's move to the second C —
Context.
slides.image_prompt: Section Header: 2. Context

slides.narration:
Context tells the Al why you're asking and
who the audience is.
It helps the Al adopt the right perspective.
slides.image_prompt:
Visuals of audience types (e.g., student,
professional, lifestyle blogger)

slides.narration:
For example: “Write a short blog post for a
lifestyle blog that focuses on sustainable
living.
Explain the top 3 benefits of owning an
electric car for someone living in a city."
slides.image_prompt: Screen close-up: user adding context

slides.narration:
Adding context makes the response more
tailored.
It understands the purpose and audience.
slides.image_prompt:
Side-by-side: previous output vs new
output

slides.narration:
Finally, let's look at the third C —
Constraints.
Constraints act like rules.
They guide the response by defining
length, format, or style.
slides.image_prompt:
Section Header: 3. Constraints
Clock icon, word count icon, style guide
visuals

slides.narration:
For example:
Write a short blog post under 400 words for
a lifestyle blog.
Focus on sustainable living and
city-friendly electric cars.
Explain the top 3 benefits of owning one in
the city.
Use a friendly, enthusiastic tone
throughout.
End with a question to invite reader
comments.
slides.image_prompt: Screen close-up: user adding constraints

slides.narration:
Compare all three outputs now.
Adding clarity, context, and constraints
improves quality of the output significantly.
slides.image_prompt:
Three outputs shown side by side (vague
→ context → constraints)

slides.narration:
Remember: the clearer and more
structured your prompt, the better the Al's
response will be.
slides.image_prompt:
Person at laptop, smiling at improved
output

slides.narration:
Now as an assignment
Pick a simple topic like Sports, Dogs, or
Healthy Food.
• First, write a vague prompt.
• Improve it by first adding Clarity to
the prompt.
Notice the response.
• Then add a context to the prompt.
Now look at the response and
constraints step by step.
• Compare the three Al responses.
slides.image_prompt: Assignment

slides.narration:
Note down which C made the
biggest difference to the output.
